title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (items 9-11 of a list of questions inside the Teichmüller notes): Grothendieck is studying 'cartes' (regular cell decompositions, generalizing the 2-dimensional maps/dessins) and their automorphism groups.

Item 10, continued from the previous page. Claim: the automorphism groups of simply connected, locally finite regular 'cartes' are Coxeter groups. The finite ones are listed in Bourbaki (Lie, ch. IV-VI) and are spheres carrying the Coxeter-complex simplicial decomposition. According to Deligne, every simply connected regular 'carte', finite or infinite, should occur in Bourbaki, at least in the case without singularities: spherical, affine (Euclidean) and the remaining 'conical' tilings. The remaining infinite case is the one where the invariant quadratic form (the Tits/Gram form B(e_i,e_j) = -cos(π/m_ij)) has, up to sign, Lorentzian signature (n-1,1). Then the 'unit sphere' {q = -1} is a two-sheeted hyperboloid, i.e. two connected components. One sheet carries the structure (hyperbolic n-1 space, Klein model). The tiling is obtained by intersecting that sheet with the simplicial cones of the Tits cone, the translates of the fundamental chamber of G.

Modern justification:
- A locally finite regular 'carte' that is a manifold has spherical facets and vertex figures.
- Its flag group is then a string Coxeter group in which all proper standard parabolic subgroups are finite.
- So every proper principal minor of the Gram matrix is positive definite, which forces at most one negative eigenvalue.
- Hence the group is spherical, affine, or compact hyperbolic (Lannér). The universal cover is S^n, E^n or H^n tiled by Coxeter simplices.
- 'Singularities' presumably means ideal or non-locally-finite vertices, the cusped (non-compact hyperbolic) cases.

Item 11, links between the icosahedron and E8. Take α a root of T^2+T-1, so Z[α] = Z[T]/(T^2+T-1) = O_K with K = Q(√5). There is a rank-4 (Grothendieck writes 'degree 4') quadratic form over O_K: the norm form on the icosian order, i.e. the maximal order of the quaternion algebra over K ramified only at the two infinite places. Its unit group is the binary icosahedral group, of order 120. Composing this form with the trace Tr_{K/Q} gives an 8-dimensional Z-lattice, which (suitably normalized) is E8; the 240 roots arise as the 120 unit icosians and their φ-multiples. This is the classical 'icosian' construction (Tits 1980, Conway-Sloane), relating H4/the icosahedron to E8.

The final 'Mais attention : la ramification [en 5?]' is the correct caveat. The different of Q(√5) is (√5), so the naive trace of an O_K-unimodular form has discriminant 5^4. One must twist by a totally positive generator of the inverse different (e.g. Tr(x/(φ√5))) to obtain an even unimodular lattice, namely E8.
errors: 'Signature (1,...,1)' as transcribed is not literally Lorentzian; the intended meaning (the two-component 'unit sphere') requires signature (n-1,1) up to sign. The image likely reads '(1,...,1,-1)' compressed.

The claim that all simply connected regular 'cartes' come from Bourbaki holds only under local finiteness/manifold (non-singular) hypotheses. Without them one gets non-locally-finite or cusped hyperbolic tessellations and universal abstract polytopes not realized geometrically. Grothendieck flags this himself ('tout au moins dans le cas sans singularités').

Item 11: the plain composition 'form ∘ trace' does not give a unimodular lattice. A scaling by a totally positive element of the inverse different is needed, presumably what the 'attention : la ramification' warning anticipates. The note is incomplete, not wrong.

ideas.what: Automorphism (flag) groups of simply connected regular cell complexes/maps are Coxeter (string) groups; the finite ones give spheres with Coxeter-complex decomposition
ideas.modern_name: Universal regular polytopes / string C-groups; Coxeter complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Coxeter (regular polytopes, 1930s-1940s); Tits (Coxeter complexes); McMullen-Schulte, Abstract Regular Polytopes (2002)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular maps/polyhedra and their groups but not this Coxeter classification explicitly

ideas.what: Classification of locally finite regular tessellations: spherical, Euclidean, or hyperbolic according to the signature of the Tits quadratic form; hyperbolic case realized on one sheet of the hyperboloid via the Tits cone
ideas.modern_name: Tits cone / Vinberg theory of hyperbolic reflection groups; Lannér groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tits, Vinberg, Lannér; Bourbaki Lie ch. V §4 exercises

ideas.what: E8 lattice from a rank-4 quadratic form over Z[(−1+√5)/2] composed with the trace; caveat about ramification at 5
ideas.modern_name: Icosian ring construction of E8 (H4 ⊂ E8 via the golden field)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tits (J. Algebra 1980, 'Quaternions over Q(√5), Leech's lattice and the sporadic group of Hall-Janko'); Conway-Sloane, SPLAG ch. 8; Moody-Patera

missed.claim: Within his Teichmüller/dessins programme, Grothendieck juxtaposes the classification of regular maps (via Coxeter groups and hyperbolic geometry) with the icosahedron-E8 link via the golden field. This hints at viewing the arithmetic of regular maps (fields of definition such as Q(√5) for icosahedral objects) through lattices. The individual facts are classical; the juxtaposition is only suggestive and not developed.
missed.quote: Liens entre l'icosaèdre et E_8 : la forme quadratique de degré 4 sur Z[α] ... composée avec la trace, donne la forme quadratique de E_8
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: it documents Grothendieck (and Deligne's input) independently recovering the icosian construction around 1981. It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Both items are classical: the Coxeter/Tits-cone classification of regular tessellations, and the icosian construction of E8 published by Tits in 1980. The page records Grothendieck and Deligne rediscovering or recalling known material as questions in a list. Its only small interest is the correct anticipation of the ramification-at-5 normalization issue.
transcription_corrections: '(le cas semblerait très [?] identique ?)' is probably '(ce cas semblerait "hyperbolique" ?)' or similar, which fits the following discussion of Lorentzian signature. Uncertain.
'le siège de la [-dite-] structure[?]' may read 'le siège de la carte' (word after the strikeout is unclear).
Last line: 'Mais attention : la ramification' is followed by a small addition below the line, plausibly 'en 5'.
'forme quadratique de degré 4' is meant as rank 4 over Z[α] (giving rank 8 over Z).
